newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudanese rebels denounce "plot to kill Afewerki".
newsitem.headline: Sudanese rebels denounce "plot to kill Afewerki".

text.p: The Eritrea-based Sudanese opposition alliance on Tuesday denounced what it said was a plot by Khartoum's Islamic-backed military government to assassinate President Isaias Afewerki.

And in the Kenyan capital Nairobi, the Eritrean embassy issued details of the so-called plot revealed by Asmara on Monday and said the tiny but militarily powerful Red Sea state was taking the matter "very, very seriously."

Eritrean Foreign Minister Haile Woldensae on Monday told a news conference in the capital Asmara that Khartoum had planned to carry out the assassination through an agent it had infiltrated into the ranks of the exiled National Democratic Alliance (NDA) of Sudan.
The Asmara-based NDA is made up of Sudanese rebel groups in exile fighting to overthrow the government in Khartoum.
On Tuesday, NDA "foreign secretary," Mansour Khalid, denounced the plot and gave more details on how it was to be executed.
"The NDA denounces the plot by the NIF (Sudan government) to assassinate President Isaias Afewerki," Mansour said.

An Eritrean government statement said the would-be-assassin, a Captain Nesredin Babakar Al Khairat currently being held by NDA security, left Khartoum in November last year to infiltrate the NDA in Asmara and had been given until April this year to carry out the assassination of Isaias.

"The captain was given until April 30, 1997, to execute the operation and to return to Khartoum by May 10, 1997 at the latest," said the statement. But it said the captain, said to be a senior officer in Sudanese intelligence, was arrested on April 20 after his cover was blown.
At the news conference on Monday Haile directly accused Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir and spiritual leader Hassan al-Turabi of authorising the operation.

"This heinous crime was conceived at the highest levels of the NIF regime, with explicit orders given to the terrorist from senior government officials including Turabi and General Omar Al-Bashir, head of state," said Haile.
Haile said Eritrea would file a complaint with the United Nations.
Khairat is being held by the NDA, which includes veteran guerrilla leader John Garang's Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
The SPLA has been fighting the government for almost 13 years for autonomy of the mostly Christian and animist south.
Some countries in the region, backed by the United States, accuse Khartoum of harbouring radical Islamic groups who export their brand of revolution.

Relations between Ethiopia and Sudan have been strained after Ethiopia accused Khartoum of sponsoring three gunmen involved in a June 1995 assassination attempt against Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa.
